question: To visualize the global transcriptomic organization of 568,654 high-quality single cells from the developing and adult mouse visual cortex across developmental stages from embryonic day 11.5 (E11.5) to postnatal day 56 (P56), project cells into a two-dimensional Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) space and color cells by the 15 major cell classes to reveal class-level clustering structure and relationships among neuronal, progenitor, and non-neuronal populations.

analyse_plan.Objective: Visualize the global transcriptomic distribution of mouse visual cortex cells across developmental stages and assess whether cells assigned to the same major class occupy coherent regions in low-dimensional transcriptomic space.
analyse_plan.Validation Checks: Verify that only high-quality scRNA-seq cells retained after quality control are included in the visualization. Confirm that all cells are annotated using the final class-level taxonomy. Ensure that major neuronal, progenitor, and non-neuronal populations form visually separable regions in UMAP space. Check that displayed class labels are consistent with the hierarchical taxonomy reported in the study.
analyse_plan.Steps: 1. Load Data: Load the filtered scRNA-seq expression matrix and class-level annotations for 568,654 high-quality mouse visual cortex cells spanning developmental stages from E11.5 to P56. 2. Preprocess Expression Matrix: Normalize gene-expression values and select highly variable genes for downstream dimensionality reduction. 3. Perform Principal Component Analysis: Reduce the dimensionality of the normalized transcriptomic matrix using principal component analysis to capture major sources of transcriptional variation. 4. Compute UMAP Embedding: Apply Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) to the reduced transcriptomic representation to generate a two-dimensional embedding of all cells. 5. Assign Cell-Class Labels: Label each cell according to the 15 major cell classes defined in the hierarchical transcriptomic taxonomy. 6. Generate UMAP Visualization: Plot all cells in the two-dimensional UMAP space and color cells according to cell-class identity to visualize transcriptomic organization and class-level separation. 7. Save Key Results: Save the UMAP coordinates, class annotations, and rendered class-colored UMAP visualization for downstream analysis and presentation.

key_analysis_results: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) visualization of 568,654 high-quality scRNA-seq cells from the mouse visual cortex across developmental stages from E11.5 to P56 reveals 15 major cell classes occupying distinct regions in transcriptomic space.

Neuronal populations, including glutamatergic neurons, GABAergic neurons, Cajal-Retzius glutamatergic neurons, and immature neurons, form related but separable regions in the UMAP embedding, whereas non-neuronal populations including astrocyte-ependymal cells, oligodendrocyte precursor cell-oligodendrocyte populations, immune cells, vascular cells, and glioblast populations occupy distinct transcriptomic regions.

Neuroepithelial cells, radial glia, and intermediate progenitor populations form connected progenitor-associated regions in the UMAP embedding and extend toward immature neuronal populations, consistent with continuous developmental transitions during cortical differentiation.
key_analysis_conclusions: Major cell populations in the developing and adult mouse visual cortex exhibit distinct transcriptomic identities that can be resolved at the class level using low-dimensional transcriptomic embedding.
Transcriptomic organization in UMAP space supports the hierarchical cell-type taxonomy and reveals clear separation between neuronal, progenitor, and non-neuronal lineages.

The spatial continuity between progenitor populations and immature neuronal populations in transcriptomic space is consistent with progressive developmental diversification during cortical development.

summary_report.abstract: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) visualization of 568,654 high-quality scRNA-seq cells from the developing and adult mouse visual cortex reveals the global transcriptomic organization of 15 major cell classes across developmental stages from E11.5 to P56. Distinct transcriptomic regions corresponding to neuronal, progenitor, and non-neuronal populations support the class-level hierarchical taxonomy of cortical cell types.
summary_report.methods: High-quality scRNA-seq cells from the mouse visual cortex spanning developmental stages from embryonic day 11.5 (E11.5) to postnatal day 56 (P56) were collected after quality-control filtering. Gene-expression matrices were normalized and reduced using principal component analysis. Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) was applied to generate a two-dimensional transcriptomic embedding of all cells. Cells were colored according to the 15 major cell classes defined in the hierarchical transcriptomic taxonomy.
summary_report.results: The UMAP embedding of 568,654 high-quality scRNA-seq cells reveals distinct transcriptomic regions corresponding to 15 major cell classes in the mouse visual cortex. Glutamatergic neurons, GABAergic neurons, immature neurons, and Cajal-Retzius glutamatergic neurons form related neuronal regions, whereas astrocyte-ependymal cells, oligodendrocyte precursor cell-oligodendrocyte populations, immune cells, vascular cells, and glioblast populations occupy separate non-neuronal regions. Neuroepithelial cells, radial glia, and intermediate progenitor populations form connected progenitor-associated regions that extend toward immature neuronal populations.
summary_report.discussion: The global transcriptomic organization visualized by UMAP supports the hierarchical classification of cortical cell populations across development. Distinct transcriptomic separation among major neuronal, progenitor, and non-neuronal populations indicates robust class-level molecular identities, whereas the continuity between progenitor populations and immature neuronal populations is consistent with progressive developmental diversification during mouse visual cortex development.
